subject: Write the free prose findings into the claims ledger (12 sections)
description:
TWELVE prose-only findings, all free, all sourced. These go to sections-drafts/ as BULLETS (never prose -- bullets-first rule) and to writing-notes/ for placement. Several STRENGTHEN existing choices, which makes them defensive citations rather than corrections.

STRENGTHENS AN EXISTING CHOICE (cite and claim it):
  13.8 -- the repo scores a SINGLE month at exactly H=3 (test.iloc[HORIZON-1]), sidestepping the mixed-horizon-variance problem the book names. 'That is a deliberate strength and the prose should claim it' -- currently justified only as 'the horizon contract'.
  5.10 -- the repo tunes on WMAPE where the book recommends RMSE, but tunes TWICE, once per objective, because WMAPE and median APE are minimised by different functionals. 5.8 supplies the theory (MAE->median, RMSE->mean). 'The deviation is principled, not an oversight. Say so explicitly.'
  9.10 -- 'AICc cannot be used to compare between ETS and ARIMA models'; test-set/CV comparison is the correct method across families. A direct endorsement of SRQ1's held-out-test design.
  9.9 -- 'when comparing models using a test set the comparisons are always valid', so cross-differencing-regime comparisons are legitimate.
  6.2 -- five judgmental principles map one-to-one onto SRQ4's controls (prompt consistency = 'systematic approach'; capability notes = checklists; typed tool = 'document and justify'; run log = 'systematically evaluate'; planner/forecaster split = 'segregate forecasters and users'). Sources the v6 schema from OUTSIDE the ML literature. The PBS case study is 'the thesis's own finding in miniature'.
  6.7 -- judgmental adjustment maps onto the B->C increment; the book's condition for adjustment helping (genuine extra information, not pattern-reading) is what B->C measures. TFC example is a precedent for over-forecasting in A_llm_plain.

CORRECTS OR COMPLETES A JUSTIFICATION:
  13.3 -- positivity belongs on the log scale, not post-hoc clipping: 'post-hoc clipping is nowhere endorsed'. Ch5 already calls its upper bound 'a departure from that preference' -- the book CONFIRMS the departure is real and names the principled alternative (scaled logit; quantiles preserved under monotonic transformation).
  5.6 -- back-transformed forecasts are MEDIANS, not means, and 'medians do not add up, whereas means do'. So brand forecasts must not be summed to a category total without bias adjustment (y_hat = exp(w)*[1+sigma^2/2] for lambda=0). SRQ2-touching; P0048 already has this open as an SRQ2 item -- 5.6 is the citation AND the formula. ALSO confirms the split-conformal interval being formed in log space then exponentiated.
  3.2 -- uniform log1p is implicitly a MULTIPLICATIVE SEASONALITY commitment ('y = S x T x R is equivalent to log y = log S + log T + log R'). Very likely correct for retail beverage demand, but the thesis nowhere states what the transform commits it to. CONFIRMS the choice, REFINES the justification.
  2.3 -- 'identify the time series patterns in the data, and then choose a method able to capture the patterns properly'. The missing piece is the LINK from identification to method choice. Also: a CYCLIC claim is unsupportable at 39-46 months (cycles are 'usually at least 2 years'), so audit the prose for the word.
  2.4 / 2.5 -- seasonal STABILITY ACROSS YEARS is never checked, yet peak_month is computed from pooled means. 2.4 is 'especially useful in identifying years in which the pattern changes'; 2.5 shows 'changes within particular seasons'. Also flags multiple seasonal periods, which matters if the Nielsen 4-4-5 calendar induces a second cycle.
  11.1 / 11.3 -- the panel is exactly a mixed hierarchical/grouped structure, (category/brand) x market, and the thesis has never named it. Brand forecasts do not reconcile to a category total. DEFERRED as future work by the log's own instruction, BUT it is the correct vocabulary for Phase 4 (task 11), and wls_struct 'needs no residuals' so it suits judgmental base forecasts -- i.e. the LLM scenarios.

ROUTED AWAY: 5.5 belongs to BRANCH A / the Ch9-Ch10 session (Ch7's interval-communication criterion). Hand it over; do not action here.
